problem: LLMs must balance diversity and creativity in open-ended generation, but existing truncation-based sampling methods ignore the semantic geometry of token embeddings while balancing probability mass and entropy.
approach: Top-W uses Wasserstein distance over token-embedding geometry to keep the cropped distribution close to the original while explicitly trading off retained probability mass against entropy, yielding a simple closed-form update that either collapses to one token or forms a one-dimensional prefix.
contribution: Top-W outperforms prior state-of-the-art decoding approaches on GSM8K, GPQA, AlpacaEval, and MT-Bench, achieving up to 33.7 percentage point improvement and boosting both accuracy and creativity.

problem: Time-series forecasting models lag behind operational numerical weather prediction systems in capturing complex weather dynamics and extreme events, hampered by small, sparse, temporally short datasets.
approach: PhysicsFormer combines a dynamic core with a Transformer residual to predict weather states, enforcing physical consistency via pressure-wind alignment and energy-aware smoothness losses.
contribution: PhysicsFormer and other TSF models are benchmarked against operational systems across weather variables and extreme events, with WEATHER-5K, a large-scale observational dataset, supporting improved model training.

problem: Link prediction in graphs requires capturing rich topological dependencies, but existing approaches rely on explicit structural heuristics or memory-intensive embeddings that struggle to generalize or scale.
approach: PENCIL is an encoder-only plain Transformer that replaces hand-crafted priors with attention over sampled local subgraphs, extracting richer structural signals than GNNs while remaining parameter-efficient.
contribution: PENCIL outperforms heuristic-informed GNNs and ID-embedding alternatives across diverse benchmarks without node features, while remaining competitive and far more parameter-efficient.

problem: Modern recurrent neural networks struggle with long-context understanding and extrapolation due to limited memory capacity, online-only updates, and rigid memory management.
approach: Atlas is a long-term memory module that learns to memorize context by optimizing memory based on current and past tokens, overcoming the online nature of standard long-term memory models.
contribution: Atlas outperforms other modern recurrent neural networks on language modeling, common-sense reasoning, recall-intensive, and long-context understanding tasks.

problem: Dynamic submodular maximization requires maintaining near-optimal solutions with minimal adjustments at each step, but prior work only addresses insertion-only streams, not fully dynamic ones with insertions and deletions.
approach: A general framework instantiated for cardinality-constrained and matroid-constrained settings, yielding constant-factor approximations with sublinear consistency in the fully dynamic case.
contribution: First constant-factor approximations with sublinear consistency: 1/2 - O(epsilon) for cardinality with O(1/epsilon^2) consistency and 1/4 - O(epsilon) for matroid with O(log k/epsilon^2) consistency.

problem: V2V-MLLM frameworks for cooperative autonomous driving incur high communication and inference costs due to dense token-level sharing, and existing pruning methods ignore LiDAR spatial structure and multi-agent fusion.
approach: V2V-CCM broadcasts question and spatial coverage messages to enable selective token activation based on question intent and observed regions, reducing communication and inference overhead.
contribution: V2V-CCM achieves state-of-the-art performance on V2V-QA and V2V-GoT-QA while substantially reducing communication and inference costs compared to existing pruning methods.

problem: GUI agents struggle with CAPTCHA solving while specialized CAPTCHA solvers cannot handle general GUI tasks, creating a gap where no single system excels at both.
approach: ReCAP uses automated data collection with large-scale CAPTCHA interaction trajectories and self-correction training to enable GUI agents to solve CAPTCHAs via vision-language reasoning.
contribution: ReCAP substantially improves CAPTCHA-solving success over base agents while maintaining strong performance on general GUI-agent benchmarks.

problem: Full fine-tuning of LLMs is memory-prohibitive, and parameter-efficient alternatives like LoRA fail to approximate full fine-tuning performance while incurring lower costs.
approach: Think-Touch predicts parameter-group potentials at each step and updates only selected groups, theoretically recovering full fine-tuning convergence asympotically with lower cost.
contribution: Think-Touch shows that selective updates converge to stationary points under weak divergence conditions and derives rate-optimal greedy strategies, advancing low-cost full fine-tuning.

problem: Personalized text-to-image models may incorporate unauthorized data during fine-tuning, raising copyright concerns, but existing methods require intrusive modifications or access to pre-fine-tuned models.
approach: RECOVER leverages inversion robustness—the stable reconstruction of images under noise perturbations after fine-tuning—to detect unauthorized image usage without requiring pre-fine-tuned models.
contribution: RECOVER provides the first non-intrusive copyright authentication without pre-fine-tuned models, consistently outperforming existing methods across diverse scenarios.

problem: fMRI-to-text decoding is challenging because strong language priors can dominate autoregressive generation, obscuring whether the model truly uses neural evidence.
approach: BIT-LLM exposes fMRI-derived tokens as persistent key-value memory through interleaved cross-attention adapters, enabling repeated neural access throughout decoding via three-stage training.
contribution: BIT-LLM yields substantially improved captioning quality on the NSD benchmark with clear sensitivity to fMRI input perturbations, demonstrating effective brain-language grounding.

problem: Scaling LLMs increases computational overhead, and existing weight quantization methods are inefficient for memory-bound inference.
approach: S-Quant partitions weight tensors into fixed-size blocks with seed-based LFSR generation to produce basis matrices, reconstructing blocks as linear combinations with minimal stored data.
contribution: S-Quant achieves state-of-the-art performance at 3-4 bit weights and enables a 4x speedup via a custom ASIC accelerator for memory-bound LLM inference.

problem: Integrating LLMs into TTS systems improves expressiveness, but interpretable emotional control remains challenging with limited insight into internal emotion representations.
approach: SAEs are used to analyze emotion-related variation in LLM-based TTS semantic hidden states, identifying sparse latent features that enable interpretable emotion control via feature-level intervention.
contribution: Sparse latent features achieve comparable or superior emotion induction and suppression relative to global steering, with distinct features associated with specific acoustic attributes.

problem: Object removal methods that block attention in vacated regions during image generation degrade quality because the model must simultaneously reconstruct background content.
approach: AdaEraser dynamically modulates attention based on estimated object-concept presence, developing token-wise adaptive attention suppression that adjusts suppression strength across denoising timesteps.
contribution: AdaEraser achieves superior object removal performance, outperforming even training-based methods through adaptive timestep-aware suppression.

problem: Classical treatment effect measures like ATE fail to capture differences across entire outcome distributions.
approach: Sinkhorn treatment effect uses entropic optimal transport as a distributional measure, characterized as a smooth transformation of counterfactual mean embeddings with appropriate kernels.
contribution: First-order pathwise differentiability is established in general and second-order pathwise differentiability under the null hypothesis, enabling debiased estimators and asymptotically valid tests.

problem: Federated fine-tuning of LLMs on resource-constrained devices requires prohibitive computational and communication overhead.
approach: SmartFed reuses knowledge from existing LoRA modules decomposed into rank-level experts, selectively activating them based on input semantics and resource budgets via Mixture of Rank-Wise Experts (MoRE).
contribution: SmartFed significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in model performance and training efficiency on multiple benchmarks.

problem: Coding agents struggle to infer and track underspecified or context-dependent user intent in software engineering tasks.
approach: ToM-SWE pairs a primary SWE agent with a lightweight theory-of-mind agent dedicated to modeling user mental state, maintaining persistent user memory and providing suggestions.
contribution: ToM-SWE achieves 59.7% task success on stateful SWE-bench versus 18.1% for OpenHands, with 86% user satisfaction in a three-week study with professional developers.

problem: Existing benchmarks evaluate coding agents on isolated one-off tasks, neglecting temporal dependencies and technical debt inherent in real-world software evolution.
approach: EvoClaw uses DeepCommit to reconstruct executable Milestone DAGs from commit logs, enabling benchmarking of long-term software evolution where agents must sustain system integrity.
contribution: Evaluation of 12 frontier models reveals critical vulnerability: performance drops from >80% on isolated tasks to at most 38% in continuous evolution, exposing agents' struggle with long-term maintenance.

problem: Modeling dynamic dependencies from irregularly sampled event sequences is challenging when individual and population-level states evolve asynchronously.
approach: CoCLD jointly models individual latent dynamics and population-level distributional shifts in continuous-time, integrating diffusion-based latent interpolation with neural ODEs.
contribution: CoCLD effectively captures dynamic dependencies and generalizes across next-event prediction, trajectory generation, and sequential behavior modeling with sparse irregular observations.

problem: Mechanistic understanding of how few-shot prompts shape a model's function vector in in-context learning remains unclear.
approach: An n-shot function vector is shown to be well-approximated by a linear combination of example-level sub-FVs, with models contextualizing individual examples and reweighting demonstrations based on informativeness.
contribution: Causal decomposition separates Query-Key routing from Value updates, revealing that contextualization's consistent contributions arise from Query-Key alignment, especially in ambiguous settings.

problem: Efficient distillation of LLMs via structured pruning causes reasoning collapse due to uneven singular-value distribution in projection matrices.
approach: RED introduces activation-aware initialization that initializes projection matrices as channel-selection matrices, theoretically mitigating effective-rank collapse.
contribution: RED substantially recovers reasoning ability while maintaining high training efficiency and state-of-the-art general ability on Llama and Qwen series.

problem: Zero-shot LLM-generated text detection using a fixed surrogate model performs sub-optimally because surrogate-source alignment varies substantially.
approach: DetectRouter learns text-detector affinity through two-stage training, constructing discriminative prototypes and aligning geometric distances with detection scores to select appropriate surrogates.
contribution: DetectRouter demonstrates consistent improvements across multiple detection criteria and model families on EvoBench and MAGE benchmarks.

problem: Language identification systems remain brittle in low-resource and closely related language settings despite near-perfect performance on high-resource languages.
approach: UniLID uses the UnigramLM tokenization algorithm's probabilistic framing for efficient language identification, supporting incremental language addition without retraining.
contribution: UniLID achieves competitive performance on standard benchmarks, substantially improves sample efficiency in low-resource settings (surpassing 70% accuracy with five labeled samples per language), and delivers large gains on dialect identification.

problem: Sequential resource allocation with stochastic referral capacity and endogenous opportunity generation is intractable when modeling multi-round planning with high-dimensional frontier evolution.
approach: A population-level surrogate value function depending only on remaining budget and frontier size enables an exact dynamic program via truncated probability generating functions.
contribution: Planning algorithm achieves polynomial complexity in budget with robust error bounds decomposing single-round frontier error and population-level transition error.

problem: Integrating LLMs into ad auctions for dynamic creative enhancement disrupts mechanism design due to significant computational costs and non-stationary agent responses.
approach: Platform-Investment Mechanism models the system as a Stackelberg game where the platform optimizes investment via two-timescale learning and agents learn bidding via ODDB-R algorithm.
contribution: TTSL-PPO algorithm converges to Stackelberg Stationary Point, with experiments showing significant improvements in revenue, social welfare, and user engagement.

problem: LiDAR point cloud anomaly detection methods rely only on visible measurements, overlooking occlusion as a structured consequence of sensing that characterizes anomalies.
approach: COVAL intervenes on volumetric visibility during training, generating paired factual and counterfactual observations to model occlusion-induced missing regions and enforce visibility-invariant consistency.
contribution: COVAL achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard LiDAR anomaly segmentation benchmarks through counterfactual occlusion-visibility learning.

problem: Vision-Language Models fail at elementary spatial tasks like block counting due to missing coherent 3D mental representations from 2D observations, creating a spatial intelligence gap.
approach: 3ViewSense uses orthographic views as a spatial interface, decomposing complex scenes into canonical projections and employing a Simulate-and-Reason mechanism for explicit mental rotation.
contribution: 3ViewSense significantly outperforms existing baselines on spatial reasoning benchmarks with consistent gains on occlusion-heavy counting and improved stability in spatial descriptions.

problem: Verbose Chain-of-Thought reasoning in MLLMs introduces inefficiencies that hinder practical deployment.
approach: Heima condenses lengthy CoTs into a small set of abstract thinking tokens while preserving reasoning, with an adaptive interpreter reconstructing variable-length textual sequences.
contribution: Heima improves reasoning efficiency while maintaining or achieving better zero-shot accuracy, with interpreter validating that the information gap is minimal.

problem: Existing sequential strategic classification focuses on optimizing classifier weights, not on designing threshold sequences that incentivize genuine effort over dishonest actions.
approach: A multi-level promotion-relegation framework analyzes threshold design capturing inter-temporal incentives driven by agent farsightedness and skill retention effects.
contribution: Under mild conditions, a designed threshold sequence enables agents to reach arbitrarily high levels solely through genuine improvement efforts, incentivizing honest behavior.

problem: Vector quantization with standard k-means for KV cache compression suffers from centroid shrinkage, which weakens directional preservation in the k-means objective.
approach: Gain-Shape k-means (GSKM) improves directional fidelity while matching k-means l2 distortion, incorporated into Residual Quantization for sub-1-bit KV cache.
contribution: GSRQ improves 1-bit KV cache from 11.34 to 33.54 accuracy on LongBench tasks, a 22.20 percentage point gain over VQLLM.

problem: Existing diffusion and flow models rely on external models for strong semantic representations, operating on misaligned objectives with unexpected scaling behavior.
approach: Self-Flow integrates representation learning within generative framework via Dual-Timestep Scheduling, applying heterogeneous noise levels to create information asymmetry.
contribution: Self-Flow enables multi-modal training following expected scaling laws while achieving superior image, video, and audio generation without external supervision.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models have high computational cost that hinders real-time deployment, and token pruning methods indiscriminately discard critical geometric details like contact points.
approach: GridS performs task-aware continuous token resampling by adaptively predicting salient coordinates and extracting features via differentiable interpolation.
contribution: GridS achieves 76% reduction in FLOPs with no degradation in success rate, using fewer than 10% original visual tokens on LIBERO and real robotic tasks.

problem: Preference learning methods like DPO induce reliance on spurious correlations, leading to sycophancy, length bias, and goal misgeneralization in deployed models.
approach: Tie training uses ties (equal-utility preference pairs) to introduce data-driven regularization that selectively reduces spurious learning without degrading causal learning.
contribution: Unified theoretical analysis characterizes spurious learning mechanisms and demonstrates that tie training mitigates spurious reliance while preserving causal learning.

problem: The principles generating a continuous gradient of hippocampal place field sizes from discrete grid cell inputs remain unclear, but this organization suggests an inductive bias for multiscale representation.
approach: A unified framework establishes how multiscale place fields arise from frequency-dependent decay of grid cell projections, translated to HiPE (hippocampus-inspired positional embedding) in Transformers.
contribution: HiPE demonstrates effective data efficiency improvements, establishing a link between neural connectivity, activity patterns, and learning.

problem: Behavior cloning with generative policies is limited by demonstration coverage and distribution shift, and direct RL fine-tuning on large action decoders is unstable and sample inefficient.
approach: LP-DS learns a compact noise-space perturbation to improve frozen generative policies using Lagrangian trust-region objective, constraining deviation from latent prior.
contribution: LP-DS improves sample efficiency and success across RoboMimic, OpenAI Gym, and Adroit with up to 25% return improvements, validated on real Franka deployment.

problem: Post-training robustness analysis lacks a unifying framework for understanding how parameter perturbations affect model outputs across different perturbation types.
approach: Test Prediction Variance (TPV) provides a unifying framework via its trace form Tr(H_eff*C) separating model geometry from perturbation covariance.
contribution: TPV converges from training to test set in overparameterized limit and correlates well with test loss, enabling label-free pruning criterion JBR and model selection.

problem: Existing mask-guided diffusion for subtitle removal requires extensive annotations, full model fine-tuning, explicit mask sequences during inference, and cannot adapt to quality variations.
approach: CLEAR uses self-supervised prior learning to extract occlusion guidance without annotations, LoRA-based adaptive refinement for parameter efficiency, and adaptive focal weighting.
contribution: CLEAR achieves superior multilingual subtitle removal requiring only 0.77% trainable parameters with true mask-free end-to-end inference.

problem: Bilevel optimization in RL with competitive lower-level interactions (zero-sum games) lacks efficient algorithms avoiding second-order information while maintaining convergence guarantees.
approach: PANDA is a penalty-based first-order policy-gradient method based on the Nikaido-Isoda function that exploits min-max structure to avoid hypergradient computation.
contribution: PANDA converges to stationary points in O-tilde(epsilon^-1) iterations with O-tilde(epsilon^-3) sample complexity, matching best-known bilevel RL rates.

problem: Existing LLM evaluations for GPU code generation focus on single-shot generation and underplay tool use and feedback, lacking standardized evaluation frameworks.
approach: TritonGym provides a benchmark and orchestration framework that standardizes tool access via function-calls, separating model capability from workflow design.
contribution: TritonGym spans maintained operators, community samples, and out-of-distribution tasks, enabling fair comparison and facilitating progress on agentic GPU-code systems.

problem: Video forensics methods fail in realistic scenarios where AI-generated content is sparsely embedded in long-form videos, focusing only on short clips without temporal localization.
approach: MSLoc combines boundary-sensitive proposal generation for efficient scanning with MLLM-based refinement for precise boundary localization and interpretable reasoning.
contribution: TASLE benchmark comprises 12,472 untrimmed videos with manipulation patterns and rich annotations; MSLoc validates the importance of segment-level explainable forensics.

problem: Deploying robots in open-ended environments demands continual learning to adapt to new tasks while retaining prior skills, but monolithic policies face capacity constraints.
approach: Nevo-CRL maintains a fixed-capacity policy network using mask populations to selectively activate neuron outputs per task, with semantic reuse and dynamic allocation.
contribution: Nevo-CRL achieves state-of-the-art continual RL performance with neuron freezing to prevent catastrophic forgetting and importance-guided mask optimization.
